description: The Sansaar is the world we all live in. Gurbani teaches us to do good deeds in this world so that we remember Waheguru in everything we see and do.
In Gurbani, Jam is the messenger who reminds us that life on earth does not last forever. This teaches us to live honestly and to remember Waheguru every day.
Gurbani uses Keere to remind us that all living things, even the tiniest worm, are created by Waheguru and are precious to Him.
A Jant is any living being — people, animals, birds, and insects. Gurbani tells us that Waheguru lives inside every single living being and loves them all equally.
A stone is heavy and hard, yet Waheguru can cross us over even the heaviest troubles. Gurbani teaches that no burden is too great when we hold onto His name.
A mother loves her child more than anything. Gurbani compares Waheguru's love for us to the love of a mother — always caring, always kind, and always there.
Gurbani calls Waheguru our Pita — our Father. Just as a loving father looks after his children, Waheguru watches over and protects every soul He has created.
A rock is strong and does not move. Gurbani tells us that the name of Waheguru is like a rock — solid and steady — that we can always hold onto for strength.
Our hands are a gift from Waheguru. Gurbani teaches us to use our hands to do good — to help others, to pray, and to serve the Sangat with love.
